# Instructions for accurately documenting reportable workplace accidents

1. Start with the incident records.
2.
completion:
Summarize the incident.
3. Confirm the employee was on the clock.
4. Connect the accident to work.
5. Make an initial determination of severity.
6. Document the severity.
7. Re-classify if severity changes.
8. Consult a professional if in doubt1. Start with the incident records.

First, make sure the company has an incident record for every reportable accident. Reportable accidents are those that occur while an employee is on the clock, are the result of work, and result in a recordable injury.

The OSHA 300 log captures an overall summary of workplace safety and health data and requires an incident record for every work-related injury or illness.

To get started, make sure you check the OSHA change announcement that details the changes to the OSHA Recordkeeping Rule.
[https://www.osha.gov/recordkeeping/announcement-register-worker-requests](
